questions: Did the s-bend max_error fall below 0.06 m, or does it still cluster at about 0.063 m? If it still clusters there, the limit is not turn authority.
Did steering_oscillation rise above the iteration 2 level (oval 0.27, s-bend 0.43) with the narrower track? If so, does kd at 0.6 contain it?
Did the oval finish rate rise above 0.45 with the narrower track and did completion_time improve?
Did s-bend line-loss events stay near 0.9, which would mean the five-sensor row is too narrow at the bends?

intent: Keep the iteration 2 design (five sensors at ±0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg, body and wheel radius unchanged) and narrow wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m. This tests whether further turn authority removes off-track exits on the s-bend and raises oval completions. Expected result: s-bend max_error below 0.06 m, fewer s-bend line-loss events (currently 0.9), and oval finish rate above 0.45. Gains and base_speed remain the Integrator's choice.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that narrowing wheel_track and lowering mass raised oval completions from 1 to 9 of 20 trials. This iteration tests whether the same lever still gives gains at 0.09 m. If max_error on the s-bend stays at 0.06 m, the next candidate should test the sensor row (for example ±0.05 m with five sensors) or the base speed, not turn authority.
rationale: Iteration 2 (five sensors at ±0.04 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg) is the best result so far at 321. Its gain came almost entirely from the oval, where finish rate rose from 0.05 to 0.45 and mean progress rose to 0.86. The change in turn dynamics is therefore the lever that matters. Sensing is not the binding limit: widening to seven sensors in iteration 1 cut line loss but lost completions. On the s-bend, however, 18 of 20 trials still end off track with max_error about 0.063 m and 0.9 line-loss events per run, so the s-bend is still limited by how tightly the robot can turn. Narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m (with the mass drop) moved the oval from almost no finishes to 45%, which suggests more yaw per unit of PWM difference is still helping. The Integrator has already reduced kp to 3.6 and raised kd to 0.6 for this candidate to hold effective gain. I therefore make one geometry change: wheel_track 0.10 to 0.09 m, keeping mass 0.6 kg, the five-sensor row and the body fixed. This isolates turn authority again. I expect higher yaw response, more s-bend completions and max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend. The risk is steering_oscillation rising as yaw gain increases, which the Integrator's kd change should absorb. If the oval finish rate does not improve and max_error stays near 0.06 m, the next limit is base_speed (controller side), not geometry.
